A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CycleResearcher and CycleReviewer. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including the replacement of generated-paper examples and relocation of retained analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original reviewer evaluations, generated-paper assessments, ablations, human evaluations and detection experiments. These qualify independently of the fabricated experimental results inside its generated-paper examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds reviewer-score distributions, an independent reward-model evaluation and an Appendix I computational case study explicitly reported as executed.

M1.justification: The model architectures and iterative SimPO-plus-NLL training procedure remain unchanged. Appendices H–I add a demonstrated execution-assisted workflow: experimental plans go to an AI Scientist code executor, and measured results return to CycleResearcher for analysis and writing. v1 envisioned external experimenters but left execution to future work.

E1.justification: The principal datasets and paper-generation/review tasks remain. Appendix I adds an executed research scenario involving synthetic division, subtraction, addition and permutation tasks. The benchmarks named inside v1's fabricated World GPT and VLM reward-hacking manuscripts do not establish previously executed benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: The six API-based reviewer comparators and the AI Scientist comparisons are retained. Table 5 adds ICLR 2024 accepted and submitted papers as human-written reference groups within the human-evaluation comparison; their scores come from existing datasets, not the same newly conducted expert assessment.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct evaluation designs: a reward model trained exclusively on Review-5k test data for independent scoring, and executed synthetic-task experiments with specified architectures, optimization budgets and controlled variations. Separately, Section 2 changes the reported review test size from 781 to 782 and the Research-14k collection total from 7,725 to 14,911, while retaining its final training/test counts. These revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine whether CycleReviewer defaults to central scores through distribution plots, and whether CycleResearcher exploits its training evaluator through independent reward-model scoring. Appendix I replaces two simulated manuscript examples with an executed case containing data-size, scaling, initialization and regularization analyses. The existing RL/iteration/NLL ablations, rejection-sampling analysis and citation-count comparison remain.

E5.justification: Appendix I introduces learning curves titled 'Across Runs' with shaded variability bands, although run counts, seeds and the bands' statistical meaning are unspecified. The principal evaluation tables retain point estimates. v1's explicit seed and confidence-interval statements occur inside its fabricated example manuscript, not verified experimental reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes the 123B average score from 5.13 to 5.15 and acceptance rate from 21.19% to 24.28%; Table 3 also revises its component scores. Table 5 adds human reference scores of 6.4 and 5.5. New Table 9 reports original versus independent-evaluator averages of 5.36 versus 5.29 and acceptance rates of 31.07% versus 28.65%. Distribution findings and the executed Appendix I results substantially expand the evidence, while most original comparison scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The SimPO/NLL equations and proxy-MSE assumptions and derivation are retained, with the latter moving from Appendix C to E. Mathematical content changes within the replacement example: Appendix I defines generalization-gap peakness, an inflection condition, integrated area and transition duration, replacing the earlier example manuscripts' world-model/RL formulations. No new guarantee for the main framework is introduced.

C1.justification: v1's abstract and introduction claim superiority over expert reviewers and human preprints. v2 narrows these to assistance for expert evaluation and competitiveness in simulated review scores. Its conclusion restricts reviewer superiority to evaluated closed-source models. These materially qualify central effectiveness claims while retaining the framework and dataset contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly limits proxy-score evidence to scoring consistency rather than comprehensive expert judgment. Section 4.3 acknowledges that the unchanged human score of 4.8 falls below ICLR submission and acceptance averages. New discussion interprets score distributions and independent evaluation, while expanded limitations and usage guidance explain domain dependence, fabricated-result limitations and the need for human oversight.

D1.justification: The human study newly documents anonymization, PDF-to-Markdown preparation, N=100 rejection sampling, AI Scientist's 50 initial ideas and three refinements, and a one-week evaluation period. Appendices C and H–I add licensing/access conditions, JSON exchanges and execution resources of approximately $20 and six hours on one A100. Conversely, v2 removes the policy model's explicit FP8/LoRA-GA description and exact baseline reflection/ensemble counts; reviewer hardware and model-card knowledge dates are also revised.

R1.justification: The main related-work positioning is largely retained. The principal bibliography removes AgentReview, the original LoRA paper and the FP8 quantization reference; several other differences are publication-metadata updates to the same works. The replacement example exchanges RL-focused citations for grokking and generalization literature without redefining the main framework's novelty.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises claim-bearing passages, the human-evaluation explanation and ethical discussion, and standardizes the cycle terminology around 'Refinement'. It moves the reproducibility statement, reorganizes the appendices around separate usage, licensing, analysis and integration sections, and replaces two example manuscripts with one. These are substantial narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds score-distribution histograms, Table 9 and the executed example's learning curves and tables. Table 5 gains human-reference rows, Table 1 becomes a smaller wrapped display, and other tables move. The earlier Figure 4 is retained as Figure 6 with updated values; diagrams receive label/caption edits, and conference headers replace university-logo headers.

improvement.justification: v2 improves claim calibration, documents the human evaluation more clearly, and adds independent scoring and an executed research example. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies: Table 9 implies an average-score difference of 0.07 while its text states 0.14; Appendix D.2 retains obsolete 123B values; and the new example contains interpretations contradicted by its own tables. The clearer scope and additional checks support a limited overall improvement, with the strength of the new validation remaining constrained.
